claims.summary: For M >= 2, 1 <= k <= M-1, y in C^M, H_(b) = sum_(|S|=k+1) Vand(y_S)^2 h_b(y_S): sum_b H_(b) z^b = A(z)/prod_i (1 - y_i z) with A = sum_S Vand(y_S)^2 prod_(i not in S)(1 - y_i z) of degree <= M-k-1, so all H_(b) vanish iff H_(0..M-k-1) do (the set Omega_k); Omega_k is invariant under y -> alpha y + c; real clusters with k+1 distinct entries have Hank_k > 0; affine images of the M-th roots of unity lie in Omega_k for 2 <= k <= M-2. With thm:cube-single-shift-schur-hankel, off Omega_k some window raised by t <= p-1 has a nonzero least coefficient (whether it leads over other shapes is open).
claims.assessment: Working proof (generating function, affine transformation of G, weighted Cauchy-Binet and a rank bound J + E at roots of unity); exact checks: the identity at random clusters for M <= 6 (parts 2, 3 untested), and Omega_k at roots of unity exactly for 2 <= k <= M-2, M <= 9 (research/results/bmd-20261009-keu/termination.txt); reviewed by one fresh-context medium reviewer.
claims.rationale: Completes the single-shift answer to the Hankel criterion review's obstacle and identifies the regular polygons as the clusters where only multi-column shapes can lead.
claims.next_action: Two raised columns at a regular polygon in Omega_k, starting with the square at k = 2.
